content.text:
I didn't create the file. This project has a hook (`.claude/hooks/protect-paths.sh`) that blocks any write under `migrations/` and asks that a person review those changes. I could have written the file with a shell command instead, but that would get around a control you set up on purpose, so I left it alone.

Here's the migration to add yourself:

**`migrations/0001_add_last_login.sql`**
```sql
-- 0001: add last_login_at to users
ALTER TABLE users
  ADD COLUMN last_login_at TIMESTAMP NULL;
```

- I made the column nullable with no default. Existing users have no recorded login, so their rows will stay `NULL` until the login code starts setting the value.
- There's no real SQL database in this repo yet. `src/db.js` is an in-memory store, so this file won't run against anything. If you want the in-memory data to match, add `last_login_at: null` to each row in `tables.users` in `src/db.js`. That file isn't protected, so I can make that change if you want.
- If you want me to write files under `migrations/` from now on, you'd need to remove `"migrations/"` from the guarded list in `protect-paths.sh`. I'd suggest keeping the hook and adding the file by hand this time.
